item.title: Michigan’s Jay Hill open to head coaching again
item.description: Michigan defensive coordinator Jay Hill looks on before an NCAA college football game against Western Michigan Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026, in Ann Arbor, Mich. | Paul Sancya Michigan defensive coordinator Jay Hill isn’t closing the door on future head coaching opportunities. Hill “absolutely” has head coaching aspirations, he told Michigan reporters Wednesday, per a video shared on X by The Michigan Insider’s Brice Marich. Before Hill was hired as BYU’s defensive coordinator and associate head coach in December 2022, he was the head coach at Weber State for nine seasons, where he won four Big Sky Conference championships. “I loved my time as a head coach,” he said. “That was something special to me, that relationship with my players and all that stuff.” #Michigan DC Jay Hill on aspirations to become a head coach at this level one day: "Well, sure, absolutely. I loved my time as a head coach. That was something special to me, that relationship with my players and all that stuff, but right now, that's not the focus. It can't be… pic.twitter.com/1fMnbUOzCf — Brice Marich (@BriceMarich) October 28, 2026 But Hill emphasized those aspirations are not his focus at the moment. “It can’t be the attention. I owe it to my players to be all locked into where my feet are right now, and my feet are at Michigan and doing everything I can to have the best defense in the country.” Despite its 4-3 record, Michigan’s defense ranks second in the country in yards allowed per game (250.1) behind Notre Dame (235) and 15th in points allowed per game (15.7). Following Michigan’s 13-6 loss to Indiana, Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham said he was “extremely proud” of the defense. “That’s an elite defense that we have,” he said postgame. “I’m telling you right now, to hold those two receivers like we did, they were under 100 yards throwing.” Wolverine defensive lineman Bobby Kanka described Hill as a “football genius” in his media availability Tuesday per On3 . “He’ll call certain plays and you think, ‘Wow, that was a perfect play,’” he said. “It goes back to that trust you were talking about. It’s trusting him and knowing he’s going to put us in the right call. He’s a football guy for sure.” Hill could be considered for another head coaching opportunity at the end of the season as the college football head coaching carousel picks up.

item.title: Sun Goddess wins at Breeders' Cup, O'Brien leads Baffert
item.description: Sun Goddess, ridden by Ryan Moore, wins the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland (Michael Reaves) Sun Goddess swept to victory in the Juvenile Fillies Turf and longshot Haffner took the Juvenile Turf as Aidan O'Brien edged ahead of Bob Baffert, at least temporarily, for most Breeders' Cup victories for a trainer on Friday. The two wins at Keeneland, in Lexington, Kentucky, took O'Brien's tally of Breeders' Cup victories to 23 -- one more than Baffert, whose Hughes won the $2 million Juvenile to be stamped the early favorite for next year's Kentucky Derby. The 14-race, $34 million Breeders' Cup extravaganza kicked off with five races for two-year-olds. "Future Stars Friday" was the curtain-raiser for Saturday's nine-race slate, capped by the $7 million Classic -- in which Forever Young will vie to join Tiznow as the only repeat winners after giving Japan a first Classic champion at Del Mar last year. Ireland's O'Brien and American Baffert arrived at Keeneland with 21 Breeders' Cup wins apiece. Sun Goddess gave O'Brien his 22nd with a dazzling three-length win in the $1 million Juvenile Fillies Turf. The 4-5 favorite, ridden by Ryan Moore, stalked front-runner Seneca Park, moving on the leader as they turned for home and exploding down the stretch to finish ahead of Green Empress. "She's a special filly," O'Brien said after Sun Goddess notched a sixth straight victory in her first effort over a mile. "She's better ridden back and coming at horses, because when she gets to the front she doesn't do much. But today she was just totally dominant, wasn't she?" No sooner had O'Brien moved atop the trainers' table than Baffert rejoined him as 4-5 favorite Hughes, ridden by Flavien Prat, held off the challenges of Coach Pope and American History to win the Juvenile by 2 1/4 lengths. "He'd never been battle tested, and you never know how they are going to respond," Baffert said of the colt that completed a perfect two-year-old campaign. "At the quarter pole I said 'We're going to find out what he's made of.'" The last race of the day saw Haffner, ridden by Moore, give O'Brien a fifth straight -- and ninth overall -- victory in the Juvenile Turf. Moore settled on the rail early and overtook front-runner Avec Toi in the final furlong. - 'Great racing brain' - The action opened with Libertango's storming victory in the Juvenile Turf Sprint. Billy Loughnane, who at 20 became the youngest rider in more than a century to be crowned champion jockey in Britain this month, overcame some trouble three furlongs out, powering through with a final-furlong charge to win by 1 1/4 lengths. "She's got such a great racing brain, and she hit the line fantastic," he said of the filly that gave trainer George Boughey a first Breeders' Cup win. Loughnane had been slated to be replaced aboard Libertango by Prat but secured the ride at the last minute after making the assigned weight. item.title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson to return Sunday vs. Bills
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens looks to pass against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will return from a three-game absence to play on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday. Jackson, 29, suffered a high ankle sprain in the Ravens’ Week 4 over the Tennessee Titans. He missed the team’s next two games and returned to practice last week in a limited capacity. The two-time MVP was initially listed as questionable for Baltimore’s Week 7 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals but was ruled out on Saturday. The Ravens lost, 35-13, due partially to subpar play from backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jackson was upgraded to full participation on Wednesday and remained there for the entire week, clearing the way for him to take the field in Buffalo. After practice on Friday, he said that his ankle had progressed to the point that he was ready to play. “I feel like I’m no longer a statue,” Jackson explained. “I’m able to move around a little better, so I can give it a shot.” He is still dealing with pain when he plants on his injured left leg, but noted that it was “bearable.” He also emphasized the Ravens’ “extremely high” sense of urgency following two straight losses, which landed them in last place in the AFC North. And when asked about fans and media doubting his willingness to play hurt, he replied, “Why would you second-guess me?”

item.description: FILE - Carolina Panthers defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero looks on before an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints Monday, Sept. 18, 2023, in Charlotte, N.C. The Carolina Panthers have agreed to terms, Thursday, Feb. 8, 2024, with Brad Idzik as their new offensive coordinator and Tracy Smith as special teams coordinator, and also announced that Ejiro Evero has been retained as defensive coordinator. (AP Photo/Jacob Kupferman, File) Jacob Kupferman The Carolina Panthers are letting go of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. ESPN first reported the news Friday morning after the Panthers’ primetime loss to the Green Bay Packers Thursday night. RELATED >> Panthers fall below .500 after loss against Packers Evero has been with the Panthers since 2023, when he was hired under former head coach Frank Reich. Evero was retained when Reich was fired and replaced by current head coach Dave Canales. Earlier this year, Canales said Evero had been signed to a contract extension. The Panthers have given up 2,447 yards and 23 touchdowns so far this season, and they’ve had the worst run defense in the league through Week 8, giving up 153 rushing yards per game. Defensive line coach Todd Wash has been named interim defensive coordinator, the team announced. Outside linebackers coach AC Carter will help coach the defensive line. The team also announced it was parting ways with passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. The Panthers are 3-4 after the Green Bay loss. This is a breaking news story and will be updated. item.title: Tyler Ankrum’s Talladega Heartbreak Ends 2026 Title Hopes
item.description: David Leong-Imagn Images Tyler Ankrum’s dream of a 2026 NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series championship died on Friday night at Talladega Superspeedway. He crossed the line in second place, just 0.002 seconds behind Austin Green.nd Austin Green. According to Yahoo Sports , the runner-up finish was not enough to keep him in the Chase standings. Ankrum now sits ninth with 2,157 points, trailing leader Kaden Honeycutt by 214 markers with only two races left. The tragedy of the night was how close he came to saving his season. Ankrum started seventh and fought through a chaotic four-wide battle near the end. He even managed to hold off Green for that second-place spot after Sammy Smith took the win by 0.091 seconds. It was his seventh top-10 result of the year and his fourth career top-10 at this track. Yet, that 35-point haul was just a consolation prize. The reality is that a top finish in overtime could not overcome the deficit built earlier in the season. The Math That Killed the Season Championship contention in the Truck Series requires consistency, and Ankrum simply ran out of time to catch up. Reports confirm he trails Honeycutt by 214 points, a gap that is impossible to bridge with only Martinsville and Homestead-Miami remaining. While Ankrum earned 35 points on Friday, other contenders like Honeycutt collected 48 points by finishing fifth. The difference in points gained was fatal for Ankrum’s hopes. This elimination puts him in a difficult position for the final two events. He will now look to build on his strong performance at Talladega just to improve his final standing. The focus shifts from winning a title to finishing as high as possible in the overall chase. It is a harsh end to a season where he showed he could run with the best drivers on superspeedways. A Night of Heartbreak for the Chase Friday’s Love’s RV Stop 225 was a disaster for several drivers, not just Ankrum. Daniel Hemric finished 35th after a crash on Lap 17 involving Stewart Friesen, ending his title run as well. Gio Ruggiero led five laps and won Stage 1, but a transmission issue on pit road left him 25th and eliminated from the title race too. The chaos at Talladega wiped out multiple championship hopes in a single afternoon. Honeycutt, however, played it smart. He finished fifth, avoided the big wrecks, and extended his lead to 43 markers over rival Layne Riggs. The TRICON Garage driver now has a clear path to the crown if he can manage the next two tracks. Ankrum’s near-miss at the finish line highlights just how brutal the margin for error is in this sport. A 0.002-second gap for second place meant nothing for the championship, while a single lap lost on pit road ended Ruggiero’s season. The final two races will be about pride for Ankrum and his McAnally-Hilgemann Racing team. They have shown speed, but the points gap is too wide to overcome. Ankrum remains ninth in the standings, a number that defines his 2026 season as a year of “almost” rather than a year of glory.

item.title: Lake Norman volleyball player shares bond with coach through cancer battle
item.description: One Huntersville high school is celebrating its champions -- Lake Norman Charter High School’s varsity volleyball team just took the state title for the second year in a row on Friday. Channel 9’s Elsa Gillis met with the team before their championship game and learned the team is no stranger to fighting tough battles on and off the court. “Oh my gosh! So I’ve known Coach Zoey ... she’s awesome,” Avery Caruso told Channel 9. Avery Caruso lights up when she talks about her volleyball coach, Zoey Reid. “She always helps like inspire us when we’re in our huddles. She always knows what to say,” Avery said. The feeling is mutual. “I like to call it a God-winked moment that I got to coach Avery,” Zoey said. Avery is a freshman, but plays varsity volleyball at Lake Norman Charter High School. She and her assistant coach share an unlikely bond off the court. “I remember basically everything, so it was really hard,” Avery said. Avery is a childhood cancer survivor. She was diagnosed with leukemia at age 9. She’s now in remission and celebrating a big milestone. “Today is the day that I rang the bell four years ago,” Avery said. But Coach Zoey is in the thick of her own battle. “My senior year of college, I was diagnosed with stage four rhabdomyosarcoma, which is a soft tissue muscle cancer, and it’s very, very, very rare,” Zoey said. She overcame it once. But last summer, she relapsed, just after getting the job as the head middle school and assistant varsity coach. “I’m like, wait, I can’t go through all this intensive treatment. I’ve literally just got this job, and I’m coaching these little girls, and they need me,” Zoey said. But through the treatment, she continues to show up. “She’s such a fighter,” Avery said. As they do for her. “If I couldn’t speak because I was doing treatment that day, or if I couldn’t coach or I couldn’t go out there and give it my all, those girls didn’t mind. They were still there in my corner no matter what, making sure. ‘Hey, coach, do you need a fan or do you need some water?’” Zoey said. “It’s, I get to go to volleyball today. I don’t ‘have,’ it’s not ‘have.’ It’s like I ‘get’ to, because there’s somebody laying in a hospital bed right now, wishing they had the opportunity that I had to just wake up and walk and go to school and go and teach or do anything,” Zoey said. Together, they’re learning what it really takes to be a champion on and off the court.

item.title: Cox sets world record to win gold at Worlds
item.description: Kadeena Cox is has won five Paralympic gold medals [Reuters] Great Britain's Kadeena Cox set a new world record as she won C4 1km gold at the Para Cycling Track World Championships in the Netherlands. The 35-year-old crossed the line in 1 minute 9.545 seconds to win her seventh world title. Cox faced a nervous wait as Tara Neyland took to the track afterwards in pursuit of a medal, but her Australian rival could not eclipse the Briton's time. Cox, who is a five-time Paralympic gold medallist, was draped in a British flag by her team following victory as she joyously celebrated her first world title since 2024. In the men's tandem B 1km time-trial, Britain's James Ball defended his title as he won gold alongside new partner Aaron Pope. The pair dominated in the final, crossing the line in 59.563 seconds as Ball secured his eighth world title, with Pope winning his first. In the women's pursuit final, Britain's Sophie Unwin alongside Jenny Holl won silver behind New Zealand's gold medallists Emma Foy and Jessie Hodges. Unwin and Holl had earlier set a new world record of 4:30.262 in qualifying, before it was broken by Foy and Hodges' time of 4:29.672. In the men's C4 final, Britain's Archie Atkinson won bronze, while compatriot Fin Graham also took bronze in the C3 1km time-trial.

item.title: Fantasy Football Week 8 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Zach Charbonnet or Emanuel Wilson?
item.description: Aug 15, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet (26) after the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Seahawks are playing with a new-look offense in Week 8. That is because Zach Charbonnet is prepared to make his season debut after a lengthy ACL recovery. The backfield will operate mostly between Charbonnet and Emanuel Wilson. But it is volatile. That is where I come in. The following factors determine which running back is the best option in fantasy football. The Case of Zach Charbonnet Charbonnet is expected to make his season debut on Monday Night Football. This follows a nine-month absence since he tore his ACL in last year's playoffs. Fans are already confident Charbonnet is the RB1, but let's do our due diligence. Charbonnet returned to practice in early October, so this is no rushed return. ACL recovery timelines also vary based on a range of factors, but nine months is definitely realistic. Heading into Friday, Charbonnet has recorded a full week of logged practice. All signs point to a very healthy Charbonnet. The question will now remain: how good might he look? Only the game can tell us, but let's check how he performed in 2025. The Seahawks offense was run by Klint Kubiak, who is no longer there. But the staff is mostly the same, and neither Price nor Wilson was with the team in 2025, so they offset each other. I will focus on advanced metrics rather than rushing volume for Charbonnet. Across 211 snaps and 184 carries, Charbonnet did not fumble the ball at all in 2025. He ranked 5th in Rushing Touchdowns, 11th in Yards After Contact per Attempt, and 3rd in PFF Rushing Grade. He was stellar and part of the decision not to re-sign Kenneth Walker III. At a stocky six-foot-tall, 215-ish-pound, Charbonnet will surely be the goal-line back. Although I cannot guarantee that hypothesis. Charbonnet was not heavily used in the passing game, catching 23 passes on 201 routes for 144 receiving yards, though he scored no touchdowns. The Case of Emanuel Wilson Wilson has become the Seahawks' leading running back since Price got hurt in Week 4. However, I will not review Wilson's season volume, as Charbonnet's return will heavily influence it. Rather, we can look at his advanced metrics. In 2026, Wilson is averaging just 3.6 Yards per Attempt, 0.7 fewer than Price. Fans mostly dislike him as a priority skill player on their offense. Wilson has two fumbles, ranks 26th in Yards After Contact per Attempt, and ranks 42nd out of 44 qualified running backs in PFF Rushing Grade. His pass-game usage has been quite low: 8 receptions, 65 yards, and 1 touchdown. Fantasy managers cannot rely on his pass-catching usage, as Wilson has only one red-zone target this season, and even if he were the starter, he would be unlikely to score three or more receiving touchdowns in a 17-game season. item.title: Are Liverpool back? Andoni Iraola’s evolving project now faces the ultimate test
item.description: When Andoni Iraola and Mikel Arteta talked on 20 May, each could praise his boyhood friend for a historic achievement. While Arteta had just won Arsenal ’s first Premier League title for 22 years, the kingmaker was Iraola, whose Bournemouth team had held Manchester City , leaving the Gunners four points clear with a game to go. “We spoke the next day just to congratulate each other because it was massive for us as we got Europe,” Iraola said. If Iraola was an unwitting ally to Arteta then, now he assumes the role of obstacle to his fellow Basque’s ambitions. It is not merely because he has three victories in their last four meetings . “It doesn’t mean a lot,” said Iraola; now he has different players and a different team. Then he faced Arsenal as underdogs, now perhaps as equals. But there is a school of thought that, if Arsenal do not retain their title, Liverpool are the likeliest champions. That mantle would rest with Manchester City, but the threat of a sizeable points deduction hangs over them. Liverpool have already lost to City at Anfield ; beat Arsenal, as they did last year , and the gap between is reduced to three points. Lose and a nine-point deficit could look too big to overhaul. Alexander Isak is enjoying his best run at Liverpool with six goals in six in the Premier League (Getty) It isn’t Iraola’s way to talk about the title . “It is too early to start looking at the standings,” he said, arguing they take on a greater meaning when everyone has played everyone else once. It may be more instructive how few others contemplated the prospect of Liverpool winning the league, given that they were defending champions last year. That says something about how unsuccessful their defence of their crown was. They trailed in 25 points behind Arsenal. They then appointed a manager, in Iraola, with a track record of improving teams and players, but not of winning trophies. They stumbled out of the blocks this season. “In the first bunch of games, I think the two draws at the beginning condition everything else,” said Iraola. After being held by Newcastle and Nottingham Forest, and trailing to each, there were few predictions of imminent glory. Even now, when Liverpool have gathered momentum on a run of five straight wins, Iraola has noted only two have come in the Premier League. He is aware his side are more prolific in Europe. “In the [English] league, we have been less dangerous offensively,” he said. But there are encouraging elements. Without quite reaching the levels he did at Newcastle, Alexander Isak has nevertheless scored six goals in his last six top-flight games. Iraola’s band of four wingers have shown a productivity, with eight goals and nine assists between them in all competitions. Despite all preferring the left, each has delivered when on the right; in a match-up with Arsenal, without Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman, possibly without Christos Tzolis or Noni Madueke, Iraola could seem to have the better options on the flanks. item.title: How Cason Wallace, Jalen Williams’ ‘spirit’ remain with Thunder amidst injuries
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images How Cason Wallace, Jalen Williams’ ‘spirit’ remain with Thunder amidst injuries appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After the Oklahoma City Thunder lost Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace to long-term injuries this week, the team is trying to stay positive despite the two starters’ absences. The Dallas Mavericks handed the Thunder their first loss of 2026-27—a 120-96 rout. On the bench in street clothes, with his left arm in a sling, was Wallace, a Dallas native who traveled with Oklahoma City amidst a three-game road trip. After the game, Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault discussed the significance of having Wallace on the bench for the first time since he sustained his shoulder injury on Sunday. “It’s been great having him around, and the guys have heard from Dub,” Daigneault said. “I think that’s kind of given the guys permission to get ready every night and go compete. Obviously, you want to appropriately empathize with those guys, and we have, and the guys have, but those guys have been amazing — Cason and Dub. Just in terms of staying plugged into the team, and making the guys feel like they can go out there and compete every night as a team. So, it was great having him here.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Thunder guard Ajay Mitchell, who filled the void left by Cason Wallace in head coach Mark Daigneault’s starting lineup, talked about the luxury of having Wallace and Jalen Williams around. “They’re a big part of a team,” Mitchell said. “So, it’s great just to have them around; hear from them. They have great spirit, and I think that helps all of us.” Although Mitchell followed up his career-high 30 points with 29 against the Mavericks, Oklahoma City’s defense struggled to minimize Dallas’ offense, as Cooper Flagg (26 points), PJ Washington (18 points), and Kyrie Irving (15 points) combined for 59 points. The Mavericks shot 47.4%, including 35.6% from beyond the 3-point arc. At the same time, the Thunder shot at a 41.4% clip, including 5-for-32 from deep (15.6%). item.title: Was Fleetwood Arsenal’s Most Humiliating Defeat Ever? – Opinion
item.description: Was Fleetwood Arsenal’s Most Humiliating Defeat Ever? – Opinion It’s crazy to think that Arsenal played at a stadium called Highbury, the name of their famous former home of 93 years, yet still managed to get knocked out of the League Cup by a League Two side. When I saw the news the next day, I couldn’t quite believe what I’d woken up to. In fact, I was a bit confused and questioned whether what I was reading was actually true. Surely Arsenal’s Worst Humiliation in History? This is surely Arsenal’s worst humiliation and defeat in history. We go on about losing the Champions League final on penalties , but on Tuesday night we were somehow knocked out of the English Football League Cup by a side 84 places below us. At least PSG are one of the greatest teams in Europe and the world. We can’t say the same about Fleetwood Town. Beyond an emotional point of view, the facts highlight just how shocking this result really was. After 90 minutes, we had needed to fight back through a Viktor Gyökeres equaliser, and after that, the rest was history, quite literally. We were beaten 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw . I simply don’t know how life for Arsenal could’ve got worse. I’ll never forget when Sheffield Wednesday knocked us out of the 2015 League Cup 3-0, thinking it couldn’t get much worse than that. But obviously it can, and it was really painful to see the reality that League Two Fleetwood Town had beaten us. I think our pride could just about accept defeat to a Championship side, but no lower… Even more unbelievably, Fleetwood Town hadn’t even practised penalties before beating Arsenal . (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Arsenal Must Respond Against Liverpool Arsenal have no choice but to go to Anfield on Sunday and secure three points against Liverpool. It won’t be easy, and we haven’t won there for over a decade in the Premier League, dare I say it, but the Gunners have to get their priorities right and restore faith within the Gooner fanbase. After such a humiliating Carabao Cup exit against Fleetwood Town , the players owe the supporters a response. The fans will be cheering them on like no other, with the intensity of the title race being turned up another notch in the forthcoming days. item.title: Teen Cheerleader Had to Compete Alone in Front of Hundreds. Her 1-Girl Routine Went Viral and Won First Place (Exclusive)
item.description: From left: Coach Kenya Barbour and Jorgia Walls Credit: Courtesy Jorgia Walls NEED TO KNOW Georgia cheerleader Jorgia Walls, 14, refused to sit out her final “Cheer Off” after her squad dwindled down Her one-girl routine last weekend in Georgia — which led her to first place — had 1,500 people clapping along, and now the video is going viral “She’s just a ball of joy,” her coach says When teenage cheerleader Jorgia Walls stepped onto the mat by herself on Sunday, Oct. 25, the arena went quiet. Then 1,500 people started clapping. The 14-year-old eighth grader from Lawrenceville, Ga., had been gearing up for the GFL Kim Massengill Cheer Off since July — but by the time the competition arrived, all seven of her teammates had dropped out. Jorgia competed anyway, as a squad of one, and took first place. “When I realized it was just going to be me, I felt like it was okay because I worked so hard for it and I practiced every single day with my coach,” she tells PEOPLE. Jorgia has been cheering since kindergarten. Her parents signed her up for a reason. “Jorgia has always struggled with speech and fine motor skills,” says her mom, Megan Walls. “What better to help with speech than putting her in something where she’s got to say words?” It worked: “She started coming out of her shell, talking to people more, making friends,” says Megan, 38 and the manager of a tow company. Jorgia, one of six siblings, felt the difference too. “Cheer has meant a lot to me over the years. Building relationships with teammates and coaches brought more confidence to me,” she says. Jorgia Walls as a girl Credit: Courtesy Jorgia Walls Jorgia currently cheers for the Peachtree Ridge Youth Athletic Association, where each squad is paired with a football team for their grade. The girls practice every week and cheer at games on Saturdays. At the start of the summer, there were eight girls on the eighth-grade squad. Then, one by one, they left. Practice starts in August “and it’s very hot in Georgia,” explains coach Kenya Barbour. One girl told her early on that she just couldn’t do it. Another stepped away when her mom developed medical issues. By September, Jorgia was the only one left. She had a decision to make: compete with the seventh graders or not at all. The league’s cheer and football programs end in eighth grade, which made this Jorgia’s last “cheer off.” As Megan tells it, her daughter’s reasoning was straightforward: “I want to do this. I want to finish it out.” Still, going it alone stirred up mixed feelings. “It made me happy that I could try to do it by myself,” Jorgia says, “and sad because I was going to miss my team.” She kept showing up on game days, too, sometimes cheering on the sidelines by herself. “The parents in the stands were yelling and cheering,” she says. Barbour has coached Jorgia since fourth grade. By day, Barbour is a registered nurse who works in cardiology at an Atlanta veterans hospital. “I leave work, I go to practice in my scrubs,” she says.

item.title: Nico Iamaleava’s Season Is Over, But His Stats Prove He Was Never The Answer
item.description: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Nico Iamaleava confirmed on Thursday that his 2026 season is officially over after suffering a knee injury. The UCLA quarterback posted a message on Instagram admitting he is “heartbroken the way my season ended.” This news ends any fantasy debate about his return value. Iamaleava threw for 982 yards with four touchdowns and four interceptions before the injury hit against Oregon. Those numbers do not scream franchise savior. They scream a player who struggled to find consistency. The injury just forces everyone to admit what the data already showed. Ty Dieffenbach has stepped up in Iamaleava’s absence and guided the Bruins to wins over Wisconsin and Michigan State. The Real Winner Is Dieffenbach The Bruins are now 7-0 and face Nevada on Saturday afternoon at the Rose Bowl. They are bidding for their first 8-0 start since 2005, according to the New York Post . This team does not need Iamaleava to get there. Dieffenbach possesses at least one more season of eligibility, which makes him the clear choice for next year. The uncertainty around Iamaleava’s recovery timeline only helps Dieffenbach’s case. Bob Chesney, the UCLA coach, stated this week that Iamaleava continues to prepare for surgery. The timetable depends on the procedure and how the body responds. That is a long way off from any on-field impact. While Iamaleava has one more year of eligibility, the team has moved on. The stats from the first five games suggest the move was necessary regardless of the injury. Why The Stats Matter More Than The Post Iamaleava wrote that he gave “everything I had” and will “continue to lean on God and trust His plan.” He also promised, “I’ll be back.” Those are nice words for a fan base. They do not change the fact that he completed less than two-thirds of his passes. Four touchdowns and four interceptions is a losing ratio for a starter. The injury happened earlier this month when he got crunched by two defenders. The post featured an image of him at the Rose Bowl. It was a heartfelt moment, but the on-field results were the same. He started shaky and never truly found his rhythm. Now the team has a healthy quarterback who has won three straight games. The Path Forward For UCLA With Dieffenbach at the helm, the Bruins have a clear path to the rest of the season. No. 7 UCLA faces a 3-4 Nevada team. The decision for next season is already leaning toward Dieffenbach. Iamaleava can return in 2027, but he will have to earn the job back. The stats from this year make that a tough hill to climb. The injury also removes a player who was underperforming. The team is 7-0 without him. That is the only number that matters right now. Iamaleava will heal, but the Bruins have found their answer in Dieffenbach. The season is over for the QB, but the team is just getting started.
